1.explanation: The overflow problem originates in Pagination.js: the class Pagination defines the root wrapper and two side-by-side divs (prefix--pagination__left and prefix--pagination__right) in its render() method. Because no overflow-x or wrapping behavior is applied in this render path (and the CSS class prefix--pagination defaults to visible overflow), the whole pagination strip extends past its container on small viewports. To fix the issue, you would update Pagination.render (or the classNames it applies) to introduce a scrollable wrapper or flex-wrap behavior (for example, adding style or class modifiers for overflow-x: auto, flex-wrap, or a responsive breakpoint), ensuring the component can scroll or wrap instead of overflowing.
1.bug_scenario: On viewports narrower than ~42rem, the core Pagination component (from carbon-components-react) lays out its “items per page” select, range text, page selector, and navigation buttons in a single row with no wrapping or scroll container. As a result, the pagination panel bleeds out of its parent container instead of becoming scrollable or wrapping on smaller screens, causing content to be clipped or overflow into neighboring UI.

2.explanation: The root of the overflow issue lives in the Pagination component (Pagination.js). Its render() method renders a top-level <div> with the class `${prefix}--pagination` and two child sections (`--pagination__left` and `--pagination__right`). All of the markup, layout classes, and overflow behavior are applied here. To fix the container overflow you will need to adjust this wrapper’s styling (or add an overflow-scroll wrapper) in the render() output. No other component skeletons (PaginationNav, PageSelector, or the config file) are directly responsible for how the default Pagination layout behaves on small viewports.
2.bug_scenario: In the attached screenshots you can see that, on small browser widths, the entire pagination control is pushed outside of its containing element. Rather than wrapping or becoming scrollable, the “Items per page” label, page‐size selector, page‐range text, page‐number selector, and navigation buttons simply overflow horizontally and break out of their parent container.
